proposal_title: Provider Result Contract Separation & Normalized Error Taxonomy
domain_specific_rationale: From a security engineering standpoint, CP-004 establishes critical boundaries by explicitly isolating synchronous transport statuses from asynchronous generation statuses and standardizing a 9-code error taxonomy. Specifically, categorizing AUTH_REQUIRED and SECURITY_CHALLENGE as POLICY_BLOCKED prevents automated bot loops from repeatedly slamming external provider endpoints, avoiding IP rate limits, automated account bans, and credential compromise. Furthermore, the contract strictly defines raw_provider_error handling, providing the structured foundation required for R14/R07 recursive telemetry redaction before logs or errors leave the privileged execution boundary.
evidence_citations: 03_repo_blueprints/R07_PROVIDER_SDK.md:Section 9 & Section 13 (Normalized error taxonomy and credential hygiene)
capability_impact: Directly preserves CAP-03 (Provider Abstraction) and CAP-07 (Security & Isolation) while upholding CAP-12 (Autonomous Error Recovery). Eliminates security anti-patterns without breaking downstream contract consumption.
residual_risk: raw_provider_error can potentially capture unredacted HTTP response headers (e.g. Set-Cookie, Authorization) or DOM diagnostic payloads returned by third-party providers. Mitigation: R07 SDK and R14 Observability must recursively scrub all raw provider errors against the token masking filter prior to central persistence or telemetry emission.
